questions.question: Find the compound interest on ₹11,000 in 2 years at 4% p.a., interest compounded yearly.
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

For a 2-year period, the **effective rate** of compound interest at 4% p.a. can be calculated using the successive percentage formula: Rₑff = x + y + (xy/100).

Rₑff = 4 + 4 + (4 × 4)/100 = 8.16%

Compound Interest (CI) = **Principal** × Rₑff / 100

CI = 11,000 × 8.16 / 100 = 110 × 8.16 = 897.60

**∴ The correct answer is ₹897.60.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Principal (P) = ₹11,000

Rate of Interest (R) = 4% p.a.

Time (n) = 2 years

**Formula Used:**

Amount (A) = P(1 + R/100)ⁿ

Compound Interest (CI) = Amount − Principal

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/81e0c8b1f982fa8c343714ce5f3a1eef7f53efa6fbe67edbfdd035b3ce744d36.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ A = 11,000 × (1 + 4/100)²

⇒ A = 11,000 × (1 + 1/25)²

⇒ A = 11,000 × (26/25) × (26/25)

⇒ A = 11,000 × (676 / 625)

⇒ A = 11,000 × 1.0816

⇒ A = ₹11,897.60

⇒ CI = 11,897.60 − 11,000

⇒ CI = ₹897.60

**∴ The correct answer is ₹897.60.**

**__Additional Information__**

Compound Interest Formula

The amount is calculated as A = P(1 + R/100)ⁿ, where P is principal, R is rate, and n is time in years.

Difference between CI and SI

For a period of 2 years, the difference between Compound Interest and Simple Interest is given by CI − SI = P(R/100)².

Effective Rate of Interest

For successive interest rates R₁ and R₂, the effective rate is R₁ + R₂ + (R₁ × R₂)/100.

questions.question: A sum of money doubles itself at a certain rate of compound interest in 12 years when the interest is compounded annually. In how many years will it become eight times of itself?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

If a sum becomes **x times** in **T years**, it will become **xⁿ times** in **n × T years**.

Given: Sum becomes **2 times** in **12 years** (x = 2, T = 12).

Target: Sum should become **8 times**. Since **8 = 2³**, the value of **n = 3**.

Required Time = n × T = 3 × 12 = 36 years.

**∴ The correct answer is 36 years.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Time (t₁) = 12 years | Amount (A₁) = 2 × Principal (P)

**Formula Used:**

A = P(1 + r/100)ⁿ, where **A** is Amount, **P** is Principal, **r** is Rate, and **n** is Time.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/08647b6af98cd77a92149b0d9d3832508ea9418813684e2f5ae36654e39cde4f.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Case 1: 2P = P(1 + r/100)¹²

⇒ 2 = (1 + r/100)¹² → (Equation 1)

⇒ Case 2: 8P = P(1 + r/100)ⁿ

⇒ 8 = (1 + r/100)ⁿ

⇒ 2³ = (1 + r/100)ⁿ

Substituting the value of 2 from Equation 1:

⇒ [(1 + r/100)¹²]³ = (1 + r/100)ⁿ

⇒ (1 + r/100)¹² × ³ = (1 + r/100)ⁿ

⇒ (1 + r/100)³⁶ = (1 + r/100)ⁿ

⇒ n = 36 years

**∴ The correct answer is 36 years.**

**__Additional Information__**

Compound Interest (CI) Formula

Amount = Principal + Interest. CI = P[(1 + r/100)ⁿ − 1].

Difference between CI and SI for 2 years

Difference (D) = P × (r/100)².

Rule of 72

To find the time required to double an investment, divide 72 by the annual interest rate: t ≈ 72 ÷ r.

Compounding Periods

If interest is compounded half-yearly, the rate is halved (r/2) and the time is doubled (2n).</p

questions.question: Aruna borrowed a sum of ₹9,000 from Jayshree at 10% per annum on compound interest, compounded annually. Find the total amount paid by Aruna after 2 years to clear all the dues.
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Effective **rate of interest** for 2 years at 10% **compounded annually** = 10 + 10 + (10 × 10) ÷ 100 = 21%.

**Total Amount** = Principal + Interest = 100% + 21% = 121% of the **Principal**.

⇒ Amount = 121% × 9,000 = 1.21 × 9,000

⇒ Amount = ₹10,890.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹10,890.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Principal (P) = **₹9,000**

Rate of interest (R) = **10% per annum**

Time (n) = **2 years**

**Formula Used:**

Amount (A) = P(1 + R ÷ 100)ⁿ

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/b06c50e41d10319260c2df99c6ca06ed2e33968baca9664b5961f440704ef877.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ A = 9000 × (1 + 10 ÷ 100)²

⇒ A = 9000 × (1 + 0.1)²

⇒ A = 9000 × (1.1)²

⇒ A = 9000 × 1.21

⇒ A = ₹10,890

**∴ The correct answer is ₹10,890.**

**__Additional Information__**

Compound Interest (CI) Formula

CI = Amount − Principal = P[(1 + R ÷ 100)ⁿ − 1].

Effective Percentage Rate

For two successive growth rates of x% and y%, the total effective rate is [x + y + (x × y) ÷ 100]%.

Difference between CI and SI

The difference between **Compound Interest** and **Simple Interest** for 2 years is given by P(R ÷ 100)².

questions.question: If a sum of money doubles itself in 10 years on compound interest, then in how many years will it become 16 times of itself at the same rate of interest?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

In **Compound Interest**, if a sum becomes **n** times in **T** years, it becomes **nk** times in **T × k** years.

Given: Sum becomes **2 times** in **10 years** (n = 2, T = 10).

Target: Sum becomes **16 times**.

⇒ 16 = 2⁴ (So, **k = 4**).

⇒ Required time = T × k = 10 × 4 = **40 years**.

**∴ The correct answer is 40 years.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Initial Sum = **P**

Time (n₁) = **10 years**

Amount (A₁) = **2P**

Target Amount (A₂) = **16P**

**Formula Used:**

A = P(1 + r/100)ⁿ

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4a57fd7e06ffbadaab8a9f3b2eab8a4879fb5cc45cd04ad8b07a6911d49a24fd.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ 2P = P(1 + r/100)¹⁰

⇒ 2 = (1 + r/100)¹⁰ ... (Equation 1)

For the sum to become 16 times (16P) in **T** years:

⇒ 16P = P(1 + r/100)T

⇒ 16 = (1 + r/100)T

⇒ 2⁴ = (1 + r/100)T

Substitute the value of 2 from Equation 1:

⇒ ((1 + r/100)¹⁰)⁴ = (1 + r/100)T

⇒ (1 + r/100)⁴⁰ = (1 + r/100)T

Comparing powers on both sides:

⇒ T = 40 years.

**∴ The correct answer is 40 years.**

**__Additional Information__**

Compound Interest Formula

The amount A is calculated as A = P(1 + r/n)ⁿt, where n is the number of times interest is compounded per unit t.

Rule of 72

A quick way to estimate doubling time is by dividing 72 by the annual **interest rate** (t ≈ 72/r).

SI vs CI for First Year

For the first year (or first compounding period), the **Simple Interest** and **Compound Interest** on the same principal and rate are always equal.

Successive Growth

Compound interest follows a **Geometric Progression (GP)** where the common ratio is (1 + r/100).</p

questions.question: A sum of money, on compound interest, amounts to ₹578.40 in 2 years and to ₹614.55 in 3 years. The rate of interest per annum, in case of annual compounding, is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

In **annual compounding**, the **amount** at the end of a year acts as the **principal** for the following year.

Interest for the 3rd year = Amount (3 years) − Amount (2 years) = ₹614.55 − ₹578.40 = ₹36.15

Rate of Interest (R) = (Interest ÷ Principal) × 100

R = (36.15 ÷ 578.40) × 100 = (3615 ÷ 57840) × 100 = 6.25%

**∴ The correct answer is 6 ¼%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Amount after 2 years (A₂) = ₹578.40

Amount after 3 years (A₃) = ₹614.55

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/632c4f7be57410cdc8df8dc0592afd07e2b25ebe6694747187e20d7b698e13be.png] 

**Formula Used:**

A = P(1 + R/100)ⁿ

**Calculations:**

⇒ A₃ / A₂ = [P(1 + R/100)³] / [P(1 + R/100)²]

⇒ 614.55 / 578.40 = 1 + R/100

⇒ 1 + R/100 = 1.0625

⇒ R/100 = 1.0625 − 1 = 0.0625

⇒ R = 0.0625 × 100 = 6.25%

⇒ R = 6 ¼%

**∴ The correct answer is 6 ¼%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Compound Interest Basics

Compound interest is calculated on the principal plus any accumulated interest. Formula: A = P(1 + r/n)ⁿt.

Successive Growth

In annual compounding, the growth between any two consecutive years (Year n and Year n+1) is simply the annual rate R% of the amount at Year n.

Comparison with SI

For the first year, if compounding is annual, Simple Interest and Compound Interest on the same principal at the same rate are equal.

questions.question: If a sum amounts to 2 (1)/(4)times the sum after 2 years on a certain rate of compound interest, compounded annually, then the rate of interest per annum is:
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

For **Compound Interest** over **n years**, the ratio of **Amount (A)** to **Principal (P)** is given by (1 + r/100)ⁿ.

Here, A/P = 2 1/4 = 9/4 and n = 2 years.

To find the 1-year multiplier, take the **square root**: √(9/4) = 3/2.

Interest rate = (Multiplier − 1) × 100 = (3/2 − 1) × 100 = 1/2 × 100 = 50%.

**∴ The correct answer is 50%.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Time (t)** = 2 years

**Amount (A)** = 2 1/4 × Principal (P) = 9/4 P

**Formula Used:**

A = P(1 + r/100)t

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/20c649db8e2acf26270a100e49305b584f3495b41ac3224ce0c1bb4a70245dd4.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ 9/4 P = P(1 + r/100)²

⇒ 9/4 = (1 + r/100)²

⇒ √(9/4) = 1 + r/100

⇒ 3/2 = 1 + r/100

⇒ r/100 = 3/2 − 1

⇒ r/100 = 1/2

⇒ r = 100 / 2

⇒ r = 50%

**∴ The correct answer is 50%.**

**__Additional Information__**

Compound Interest (CI)

CI is calculated on the principal amount and also on the accumulated interest of previous periods. CI = A − P.

Effective Rate for 2 Years

If the rate is r%, the effective compound interest rate for 2 years is (r + r + r²/100)%.

Different Compounding Periods

For **half-yearly** compounding, the rate is halved (r/2) and the time is doubled (2n).</p

questions.question: A sum of money, on compound interest, amounts to ₹5,290 in 2 years and to ₹6,083.50 in 3 years. If interest is compounded annually, then the rate of interest per annum is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

When interest is **compounded annually**, the interest earned in the 3rd year is simply the interest on the **amount** at the end of the 2ⁿd year.

Rate % = [(Difference between successive amounts) ÷ (Preceding amount)] × 100

Rate % = [(6083.50 − 5290) ÷ 5290] × 100

Rate % = (793.50 ÷ 5290) × 100 = 15%

**∴ The correct answer is 15%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Amount after 2 years (A₂) = ₹5,290

Amount after 3 years (A₃) = ₹6,083.50

**Formula Used:**

Aₙ = P(1 + R/100)ⁿ

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/9ce85c1fa50a1c3e7a8594427e675fced8b3dbf8140c89738eca2238bffda747.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ A₃ / A₂ = [P(1 + R/100)³] / [P(1 + R/100)²]

⇒ 6083.50 / 5290 = (1 + R/100)

⇒ 1.15 = 1 + R/100

⇒ R/100 = 1.15 − 1 = 0.15

⇒ R = 0.15 × 100 = 15%

**∴ The correct answer is 15%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Compound Interest for Successive Years

If amounts for two consecutive years (n and n+1) are given, the rate R = [(Aₙ₊₁ − Aₙ) ÷ Aₙ] × 100.

Difference between CI and SI

For a period of 2 years, the difference between CI and SI is given by D = P × (R/100)².

Half-Yearly Compounding

If interest is compounded **half-yearly**, the rate becomes R/2 and the time period becomes 2n.

questions.question: Find the compound interest on Rs. 80,000 at 10% per annum for 2 year
questions.solution:

Principal (P) = ₹80,000

Rate (r) = 10%

Time (t) = 2 years

**Formula used:**

A = P(1 + r/100)t

Compound Interest (CI) = A - P

**Calculation:**

A = 80000(1 + 10/100)²

⇒ A = 80000(1 + 0.1)²

questions.question: In how many months, at a rate of 6% compound interest per annum, will a sum of ₹1,200 become ₹1,348.32.?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Principal (P) = ₹1,200

Amount (A) = ₹1,348.32

Rate of interest (R) = 6% per annum

**Formula Used:**

Compound Interest Formula: A = P (1 + (R)/(100))^n

**Calculation:**

We need to find the number of months (n).

Given:

₹1,348.32 = ₹1,200 (1 + (6)/(100) )^(n)/(12)

⇒ 1.1236 = (1.06)^(n)/(12)

Taking natural logarithm on both sides:

ln(1.1236) = (n)/(12) × ln(1.06)

⇒ (n)/(12) = ln(1.1236) / ln(1.06)

⇒ (n)/(12) = 0.1167 / 0.0583

⇒ (n)/(12) = 2

⇒ n = 2 × 12

⇒ n = 24

**Hence, the number of months required is 24 months.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] __Alternate Method__** Given:

Principal = ₹1200

Amount = ₹1348.32

Rate = 6% per annum

Calculations:

A = P × (1.06)t

Start multiplying year by year until we reach 1348.32

Year 1: 1200 × 1.06 = 1272

Year 2: 1272 × 1.06 = 1348.32 

**∴ Time = 2 years = 24 months**

questions.question: Ajay received ₹41,160 for lending ₹z for 3 years at the rate of 40% per annum compound interest. What is the value of z (in ₹)?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Rate = 40% = 2/5. **Ratio** of **Principal** (P) to **Amount** (A) for 1 year = 5 : (5+2) = 5 : 7.

For 3 years, **Ratio** = 5³ : 7³ = 125 : 343.

Given **Amount** (343 units) = ₹41,160.

1 unit = 41,160 ÷ 343 = 120.

**Principal** (z) = 125 × 120 = ₹15,000.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹15,000.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Amount** (A) = ₹41,160, **Rate** (R) = 40%, **Time** (n) = 3 years, **Principal** (P) = z.

**Formula Used:**

A = P(1 + R/100)ⁿ

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/859c4b90efad59573322d91274d12af54f646006dc957b5e5b9b939e5d83cd56.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ 41,160 = z × (1 + 40/100)³

⇒ 41,160 = z × (140/100)³

⇒ 41,160 = z × (7/5)³

⇒ 41,160 = z × (343/125)

⇒ z = (41,160 × 125) ÷ 343

⇒ z = 120 × 125

⇒ z = 15,000

**∴ The correct answer is ₹15,000.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Compound Interest Formula

The amount A after n years is given by A = P(1 + r/100)ⁿ, where P is principal and r is annual rate.

Effective Rate for 3 Years

For a rate r, the 3-year effective rate is [3r + (3r²/100) + (r³/10000)]%.

Difference between CI and SI

For 3 years, the difference D = P(r/100)² × [(300 + r)/100].

questions.question: Find the compound intrest on ₹20,000 at 20% p.a for 1(1)/(2) years compounded half yearly.
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Principal (P) = ₹20,000

Annual rate of interest (R) = 20% per annum

Time (n) = 1(1)/(2) years = 1.5 years

Interest is compounded half-yearly.

**Formula Used:**

When interest is compounded half-yearly:

Rate per half-year (r) = R / 2 = 20% / 2 = 10%

Number of half-year periods (t) = n × 2 = 1.5 × 2 = 3

Amount (A) = P(1 + (r)/(100))^t

Compound Interest (CI) = Amount (A) - Principal (P)

**Calculation:**

Rate per half-year (r) = 10%

Number of half-year periods (t) = 3

Amount (A) = 20000(1 + (10)/(100))³

A = 20000(1 + 0.10)³

A = 20000(1.10)³

A = 20000 times 1.1 times 1.1 times 1.1

A = 20000 times 1.331

A = ₹26,620

Compound Interest (CI) = Amount (A) - Principal (P)

CI = ₹26,620 - ₹20,000 = ₹6,620

**The compound interest on ₹20,000 at 20% p.a for 1(1)/(2) years compounded half-yearly is ₹6,620.**

Compounded half-yearly

A = 21500 × (1.177225 × 1.085)

A = 21500 × 1.277459125

A = 27461.7161

CI = A - P

CI = 27461.7161 - 21500

**∴ The correct answer is option 2.**

questions.question: At what rate percentage per annum (correct to one place of decimal) will ₹17,280 amount to ₹23,520 in 2 years, if the interest is compounded annually?
A principal amount of ₹8,000 is invested at an annual interest rate of 5% compounded half-yearly. What will be the compound interest earned after 4 years? [Use 1.025)⁸= 1.2184]
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

For **half-yearly compounding**, the rate becomes 5% ÷ 2 = 2.5% and the periods become 4 × 2 = 8.

The **Multiplying Factor** for 2.5% for 8 periods is given as (1.025)⁸ = 1.2184.

Interest Multiplier = 1.2184 − 1 = 0.2184.

Compound Interest = **Principal** × Interest Multiplier = 8000 × 0.2184 = 1747.20.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹1,747.20.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Principal (P) = ₹8,000

Annual Rate (r) = 5%

Time (t) = 4 years

Compounding = **Half-yearly**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3549b54512dd7141a1070b61644ce09a9d283ae62bafcedd851ed1f293ec9fa8.png] 

**Formula Used:**

Amount (A) = P × (1 + R/100)ⁿ

Where R = r/2 (half-yearly rate) and n = 2t (total periods).

**Calculations:**

⇒ R = 5% ÷ 2 = 2.5%

⇒ n = 4 × 2 = 8 half-years

questions.question: A bank gives 12% per annum interest on an account. If the interest is compounded half- yearly, then _______ of the principal would have been earned more in a year as interest on the account.
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Annual interest rate (R) = 12%

Compounding frequency = Half-yearly

Time period = 1 year

**To Find:**

The additional interest earned if compounded half-yearly compared to simple interest for one year. This means we need to find the difference between compound interest (half-yearly) and simple interest for one year.

**Formula Used:**

Simple Interest (SI) = (P × R × T)/(100)

Amount (A) for compound interest compounded half-yearly = P (1 + (R/2)/(100))²T

Compound Interest (CI) = A - P

**Calculation:**

Let the Principal amount be P.

 

SI = (P × 12 × 1)/(100) = (12P)/(100) = 0.12P

Compound Interest (CI) for 1 year (compounded half-yearly):

Rate per half-year = (12\%)/(2) = 6\%

Number of compounding periods in 1 year = 2 × 1 = 2

Amount (A) after 1 year:

A = P (1 + (6)/(100))²

A = P (1 + 0.06)²

A = P (1.06)²

A = P × 1.1236

CI = A - P = 1.1236P - P = 0.1236P

Additional Interest = CI - SI

Additional Interest = 0.1236P - 0.12P

Additional Interest = 0.0036P = 0.36%

**∴ 0.36% of the principal would have been earned more in a year as interest on the account.**

questions.question: Komal invested a sum of ₹5000 at 20% per annum compound interest, componded annually. If she received an amount of ₹7200 after n years, the value of n is:
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Rate of interest = 20% = 1/5 → Multiplier for 1 year = 6/5

Ratio of Amount to Principal (A/P) = 7200/5000 = 36/25

We know that A/P = (6/5)ⁿ

36/25 = (6/5)² ⇒ n = 2 years

**∴ The correct answer is 2 years.**

**__Alternate Method__**

Given parameters in the question:

⇒ **Principal (P)** = ₹5000

⇒ **Amount (A)** = ₹7200

⇒ **Rate of Interest (R)** = 20% per annum compounded annually

⇒ **Time** = n years

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/8efbad7c51fe1cfc1809c343dc08a36f2726a8729b8ffffac213af8001f55b67.png] 

Formula for compound interest:

⇒ A = P × (1 + R/100)ⁿ

Substitute the values into the formula:

⇒ 7200 = 5000 × (1 + 20/100)ⁿ

⇒ 7200 ÷ 5000 = (1 + 0.2)ⁿ

⇒ 72/50 = (1.2)ⁿ

⇒ 1.44 = (1.2)ⁿ

Since we know that 1.2² = 1.44:

⇒ (1.2)² = (1.2)ⁿ

⇒ n = 2 years

**∴ The correct answer is 2 years.**

**__Additional Information__**

Compound Interest Formula

The final amount A for principal P compounded annually at R% for n years is given by A = P × (1 + R/100)ⁿ. Compound Interest (CI) = A − P.

Different Compounding Periods

For half-yearly compounding, R is divided by 2 and n is multiplied by 2. For quarterly compounding, R is divided by 4 and n is multiplied by 4.

Difference between CI and SI for 2 Years

The difference (D) between Compound Interest and Simple Interest for a period of 2 years on principal P is given by D = P × (R/100)².

12696 = 9600 × (1.15)ⁿ

Simplify:

(1.15)ⁿ = 1.3225

Compare powers of 1.15:

(1.15)² = 1.3225

Hence, n = 2.

**Answer: The value of n is 2 years.**
